tour.name: Mount Fuji & Hakone Private Day Trip from Tokyo: Lake Kawaguchi, Chureito Pagoda & Lake Ashi
tour.subtitle: A private day to Japan's sacred mountain with a licensed guide and car: the Chureito Pagoda viewpoint, the shores of Lake Kawaguchi, the Fuji Fifth Station when the road is open, lunch with a view, and Hakone with its volcanic valley, Lake Ashi and the red torii in the water.

tour.overview:
Mount Fuji, a nearly perfect volcanic cone 3,776 metres high, has been worshipped as a sacred mountain for centuries and painted by Hokusai and Hiroshige. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 as 'a place of worship and source of artistic inspiration'. At its feet lie the Five Lakes, and to the south-east the hot-spring resort of Hakone, set in an old volcanic caldera.

This private day from Tokyo gives you the best chance of seeing Fuji. Your guide checks the weather and cloud cover in the morning and adapts the route: the Chureito Pagoda and Lake Kawaguchi on the north side, the Fifth Station in season, then Hakone, with the volcanic valley of Owakudani and Lake Ashi. With a car, you can stop wherever the mountain appears.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 11 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Tokyo
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 400 steps up to the Chureito Pagoda, otherwise short walks

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Chureito Pagoda and Arakurayama Sengen Park.
• Lake Kawaguchi.
• The Fuji Subaru Line Fifth Station (seasonal).
• Owakudani volcanic valley.
• Lake Ashi and Hakone Shrine.

WHY THIS WORKS
Fuji often hides in clouds, especially in summer. A private car and a guide who reads the weather let you go where the mountain is clear instead of following a fixed coach route.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone who dreams of seeing Mount Fuji, photographers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer temples and history close to Tokyo, choose our Nikko or Kamakura day trips.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Fuji is most often visible from October to February, early in the morning. The Fifth Station road is closed in winter and in bad weather. A night in a ryokan with hot springs in Hakone can be added.

days.name: The Chureito Pagoda, Lake Kawaguchi, the Fuji Fifth Station, Owakudani, Lake Ashi and Hakone Shrine
days.description:
What to expect: the best views of Mount Fuji and the volcanic landscapes of Hakone, with a licensed guide, private car, ropeway or cruise, and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 7:00 and drive west on the expressway, about two hours, to the Fuji Five Lakes. Your first stop is Arakurayama Sengen Park, where about 400 steps climb through the woods to the Chureito Pagoda, a five-storey pagoda built in 1963 as a memorial to the war dead. With the pagoda in front and Fuji behind, framed by cherry blossom in April or red maples in November, this is the most famous view of Japan.

You drive to Lake Kawaguchi, the most accessible of the five lakes, and follow its northern shore, where on calm mornings the mountain is reflected in the water. From about April to November, when the weather allows, the car climbs the Fuji Subaru Line to the Fifth Station at 2,305 metres, the starting point for climbers in summer, with a small shrine and views over the lakes and clouds. Lunch is at a restaurant with a view, with hoto, thick noodles cooked with pumpkin and vegetables in a miso broth, a speciality of Yamanashi.

In the afternoon you cross to Hakone, about an hour away. You take the ropeway over Owakudani, the 'great boiling valley', a crater of steaming vents and yellow sulphur formed by an eruption about 3,000 years ago, where eggs boiled in the hot springs turn black and are said to add seven years to your life. You then see Lake Ashi, a caldera lake with Fuji on its horizon on clear days, by a short cruise or from its shore, and walk to Hakone Shrine, whose red torii gate stands in the water at the edge of the forest. Your driver takes you back to Tokyo, arriving at about 18:00, depending on traffic.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Tokyo.
09:00 – Chureito Pagoda.
10:00 – Lake Kawaguchi.
11:00 – Fuji Fifth Station (seasonal).
12:30 – Lunch with a view.
14:00 – Drive to Hakone.
15:00 – Owakudani ropeway.
16:00 – Lake Ashi and Hakone Shrine.
16:45 – Drive back to Tokyo.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If Fuji is hidden on the north side, we may start in Hakone or go to Lake Yamanaka, wherever the sky is clearer.
• The Owakudani ropeway closes when volcanic gas levels are high; we then take the Lake Ashi cruise.
• A night in a Hakone ryokan with dinner and hot springs can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Owakudani ropeway or Lake Ashi cruise, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, black eggs, hot spring entrance.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see Mount Fuji?
faq.answer: No one can promise it: Fuji is often in cloud, especially from June to September. Your guide checks conditions in the morning and adapts the route to give you the best chance. The landscapes are beautiful even when it hides.

faq.question: Is the Fifth Station included?
faq.answer: Yes, when the road is open, usually from about April to November in good weather. Otherwise we spend more time at the lakes.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 2 hours each way from central Tokyo, more on weekends and holidays. The car is comfortable and you can rest.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch with a view, usually hoto noodles or a set menu. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the ropeway, the black eggs and the pirate ships on Lake Ashi. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Chureito Pagoda has about 400 steps, but there is a road close to the viewpoint. The lakes, ropeway and cruise are easy.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight in Hakone?
faq.answer: Yes, and we recommend it: a ryokan with a kaiseki dinner and hot spring baths is one of the great experiences of Japan.

faq.question: Can we climb Mount Fuji?
faq.answer: The official climbing season is from early July to early September, with permits and booking rules. We can arrange a separate guided climb.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers and a warm jacket: the Fifth Station and Owakudani are much colder than Tokyo. Comfortable shoes for the steps.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to February for the clearest views of Fuji, early April for cherry blossom, and November for autumn colours.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
